newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Right more likely to get France into EMU - Euro MP.
newsitem.headline: Right more likely to get France into EMU - Euro MP.

text.p: A Dutch member of the Socialist bloc in the European Parliament said on Tuesday France was more likely to qualify for the single European currency under a right-wing government than the left-wing opposition.
"It seems if you're talking about EMU that we would be better off for the time being with the Gaullists than with the Socialists," Dutch Euro MP Piet Dankert told Dutch radio.

Dankert, a former president of the European Parliament, was commenting on the consequences of President Jacques Chirac's decision to call a snap parliamentary election in a bid to revitalise France so it can qualify for monetary union.
French opposition parties blasted the early poll as a ploy to usher in further fiscal austerity while hiding the failings of the centre-right government behind a rushed campaign.
Dankert said that in general terms, a victory for the French Socialists would be better for the European Union, but not when it came to monetary union.

He said that even if parties sympathetic to Chirac won the election, it was still doubtful whether he could steer France into the single currency on time, given the widespread public resistance in France to further austerity measures.
"The Socialists say, in any case, that they would cut spending by less and therefore they certainly would not meet the (monetary union) targets in time," he added.

Dankert said the French election on May 25, a few weeks after elections in Britain on May 1, would further complicate preparations for the EU's Amsterdam summit on June 16-17 when member states hope to conclude a key treaty on EU reform.
Dankert said his first thought on hearing of the French election was that the EU's Dutch presidency should "shut up shop and go on holiday" until elections in both countries were over.
